answer: Like a harbor that only shelters ships which post a deposit, an agent economy can require every identity to lock a stake bond before it may earn. The bond stays frozen while the agent works honestly, but if peers prove the identity is a duplicate, the bond is slashed like ice calving off a glacier, gone for good. Planting an orchard of a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand locked bonds, so the attack needs real money up front while honest agents risk only what they can afford to lose.
